title: Without Taser, cop says he would have used gun
article: Had Const. Ryan Naismith not already been armed with a Taser, he would have shot Michael Langan with his pistol, an inquest was told Wednesday.
Standing just five feet away and armed with a knife he refused to drop, Michael Langan posed "a danger of grievous bodily harm," Naismith testified.
Langan, 17, was shocked by a Taser and suffered a fatal heart attack following a confrontation with police July 22, 2008, on a William Avenue back lane near the National Microbiology Lab.
Naismith said he and partner Const. Michael Temple were flagged down minutes earlier by a motorist and another man who said a suspect matching Langan's description had been breaking into cars.

As the police cruiser sped toward him and came to a stop, Langan threw his jacket to the ground, then turned to face police, shirtless, his arms stretched straight out, his right hand holding a knife, Naismith said.
"I interpreted him throwing off his jacket as his intent to either fight us run from us," Naismith said.
"He had what I considered a diabolical smile on his face," he said. "There was no joking in his face, it was something I hadn't come across as a police officer."
Naismith, seated in the cruiser's passenger seat, aimed his Taser out the passenger door window and repeatedly demanded that Langan drop his knife.
Langan didn't move or drop the knife, Naismith said.
"He had every opportunity in the world to run," he said. "He stopped for us. It was at that point I believed I was in danger of grievous bodily harm. The only option was to fight."
Naismith said Langan could have easily reached through the car door window and stabbed him.
Naismith fired the Taser, its two probes landing on Langan's shoulder and stomach.
"His body seized up, he made a loud groan and fell backward to the pavement," Naismith said.

Langan was bleeding from the head, had a faint pulse and was breathing erratically, Naismith said. Naismith said he and Temple moved Langan on to his side but did not perform CPR before paramedics arrived.
Taser International lawyer David Neave asked Naismith if he thought lethal force was justified.
And what would Naismith have done if he didn't have a Taser or similar device?
"I would have used my service pistol and shot (Langan)," Naismith said.
The inquest is on recess until April 16.
